purpose.statement: Define WorkBreakdown 0.1.0 as one deterministic DevRelay module that converts approved scope into a complete set of bounded, traceable, independently executable and verifiable work-item drafts without executing work or building code.

businessObjectives.statement: Ensure every authorized requirement, architecture target, and applicable contract concern receives an explicit work coverage disposition.
Make WorkBreakdown routing, input validation, drift detection, result validation, and replay deterministic and auditable.
Allow bounded work-breakdown capabilities to be replaced through configuration without changing module semantics or generic Core.
Preserve exact lineage from approved scope through planned work while keeping graph mutation inside a trusted Core-owned boundary.

successMetrics.name: Core-neutral adapter replacement
successMetrics.measure: Compatible WorkBreakdown adapter changes requiring a product-specific branch in generic Core.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Execute adapter-swap fixtures and product-identifier scans over generic Core source.

successMetrics.name: Authorized-scope coverage
successMetrics.measure: In-scope acceptance criteria, architecture targets or changes, and applicable contract targets or changes with exactly one valid coverage disposition.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Compare canonical coverage dispositions with the exact approved invocation inputs.

successMetrics.name: Pre-adapter drift detection
successMetrics.measure: Stale baseline, disposition, repository commit, or tree-digest fixtures blocked before adapter invocation.
successMetrics.target: 100 percent with zero adapter calls and no candidate output.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Execute independent version, digest, commit, and tree-drift negative fixtures.

successMetrics.name: Complete planning provenance
successMetrics.measure: Successful work-breakdown candidates with closed domain references and a verified exact graph merge proof.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Validate candidate references, contributor ownership, checkpoint-before-merge ordering, receipt, and result graph lineage.

stakeholders.name: DevRelay maintainer
stakeholders.role: Own the deterministic module kernel, contracts, traceability contributor, and release evidence.

stakeholders.name: DevRelay workflow author
stakeholders.role: Configure and invoke WorkBreakdown and inspect candidates before approval.

users.name: Workflow author
users.description: A maintainer or integrator converting approved project scope into candidate work items for downstream analysis and execution.
needs: Detect stale inputs before work decomposition.
Produce bounded work items from approved scope.
Swap bounded adapters without changing workflow semantics.

capabilities.name: Complete scope coverage
capabilities.description: Account explicitly for every authorized requirement, architecture target, and applicable contract concern.

capabilities.name: Bounded work decomposition
capabilities.description: Convert approved baseline or change scope into discrete independently executable and verifiable WorkItemDrafts.

capabilities.name: Replaceable work-breakdown adapter
capabilities.description: Resolve one configured provider-neutral adapter binding without coupling an operation to a product implementation.

capabilities.name: Work-breakdown governance
capabilities.description: Pin exact inputs, detect drift, validate candidates, preserve evidence, and project planned traceability through a trusted contributor.

userJourneys.name: Decompose approved project scope
userJourneys.trigger: Approved requirements, ProjectOverview, architecture and contract context are ready for work decomposition.
userJourneys.outcome: A complete, validated and traceable work-breakdown candidate is ready for the separate WorkBreakdown Gate, or an explicit control outcome explains why it is not.

steps.action: Submit exact approved baselines, explicit contract and repository dispositions, pinned capability catalog, and immutable traceability context.
steps.expectedOutcome: DevRelay validates source identity and determines whether baseline state is current.

steps.action: Request work decomposition through the configured WorkBreakdown module.
steps.expectedOutcome: DevRelay state-routes the operation and resolves the exact configured adapter without model discretion.

steps.action: Review the adapter's normalized domain candidate or explicit clarification or failure control artifact.
steps.expectedOutcome: Only a complete canonical work-breakdown candidate can advance toward the gate.

steps.action: Inspect work-item coverage, provenance, validation evidence, and proposed planning relationships.
steps.expectedOutcome: The candidate is traceable and ready for approval without claiming execution or dependency authority.

userStories.need: Account for every authorized requirement, architecture target, and contract concern exactly once.
userStories.benefit: I can approve a breakdown knowing no authorized scope was silently omitted or padded with unscoped work.

userStories.need: Convert an approved baseline or approved change into bounded independently executable and verifiable work-item drafts.
userStories.benefit: Downstream dependency analysis, specialist assignment, execution, and verification receive clear actions without WorkBreakdown performing them.

userStories.need: Select a compatible bounded adapter through configuration rather than a hard-coded operation-to-product mapping.
userStories.benefit: The best available decomposition capability can change without changing workflow semantics or generic Core.

userStories.need: Know that exact current inputs were used and that planned traceability was derived through a trusted boundary.
userStories.benefit: I can audit, resume, replay, and approve the candidate without trusting adapter-authored graph operations.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Operation routing selects only a configured WorkBreakdownAdapter; Spec Kit for greenfield, OpenSpec for existing-system establishment, and OpenSpec for change decomposition are replaceable defaults rather than permanent operation coupling.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Execute adapter-resolution and swap fixtures for both operations and scan generic Core for Spec Kit, OpenSpec, operation-specific, or product-specific branches.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every in-scope acceptance criterion, architecture target or approved architecture change, and applicable contract target or approved contract change has exactly one coverage disposition: planned with linked work-item IDs, already-satisfied with rationale and current evidence references, or no-work-required with rationale and an explicit approval reference.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Validate complete, duplicate-free coverage against the exact approved scope and reject missing, contradictory, or under-evidenced dispositions.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: When an approved current WorkBreakdownBaseline and ApprovedChangePackage exist, DevRelay selects decompose-change and supplies exact current project baselines, current-work-breakdown-baseline, approved-change-package, and current-repository-snapshot to produce one WorkBreakdownChangeSetDraft.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Execute positive and negative state-routing fixtures and verify exact current-baseline and authorized-delta lineage on the change candidate.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: When no approved WorkBreakdownBaseline exists, DevRelay selects establish-breakdown for either a greenfield or existing project without reconstructing historical work, using exact requirements, ProjectOverview and architecture baselines plus explicit contract and repository dispositions to produce one WorkBreakdownDraft.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Execute greenfield and existing-project routing fixtures with ContractBaseline or ApprovedNotApplicable and RepositorySnapshot or ApprovedNotApplicable variants, and verify that no historical-work reconstruction is requested.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: WorkBreakdownGate rejects unscoped work items, uncovered authorized scope, and invalid source or traceability references, while cycle detection, missing dependencies, and impossible ordering remain exclusively in WorkDependencyGate.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run focused gate fixtures for each WorkBreakdown rejection and prove that dependency-DAG policy is absent from the WorkBreakdown gate and present only in the downstream contract boundary.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every baseline and disposition is content-addressed and version-pinned, every repository snapshot binds a commit and tree digest, and any mismatch with ApprovedChangePackage returns baseline_drift with diagnostics before adapter invocation and without a candidate output.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Mutate each pinned version, content digest, commit, and tree digest independently and verify a pre-adapter baseline_drift outcome, zero adapter calls, diagnostics, and no primary output.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: WorkBreakdown only defines candidate actions; it does not execute or build code, establish the authoritative dependency DAG, assign specialists, choose owners, estimate, schedule, track execution status, produce change sets, or claim completion evidence.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Inspect schemas, adapter inputs, output fixtures, graph assertions, and Core execution paths for prohibited execution, assignment, scheduling, completion, and dependency-authority fields or effects.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A successful operation emits exactly one primary WorkBreakdownDraft or WorkBreakdownChangeSetDraft containing work items, coverage dispositions, dependency hints, and subordinate native artifacts; explicit ClarificationContinuation and RevisionRequest artifacts support resumption, and control outcomes are decomposed, needs_clarification, baseline_drift, unable_to_proceed, and execution_failed.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Validate result contracts for each operation and outcome, including forbidden extra primary outputs, required diagnostics on drift or failure, and exact clarification and revision lineage.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The adapter declares only the approved WorkItemDraft domain fields, including acceptance-criterion, architecture and contract references; after draft validation a trusted WorkBreakdownTraceabilityContributor derives upstream-to-downstream planning edges, Core validates and atomically merges them, and ModuleExecutionRecord binds execution ID, graph revision, update digest, persisted checkpoint, merge receipt, and resulting snapshot without storing inverse or completion edges.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Attempt arbitrary adapter graph operations and invalid reference or edge types, then verify rejection; execute a valid projection and verify only planned-by, implementation-planned-by, and realization-planned-by assertions plus exact checkpoint and merge proof.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every WorkItemDraft has exactly these fields and no others: id, objective, bounded-scope, deliverables, work-type, acceptance-criterion-refs, architecture-refs, contract-refs, required-capabilities, dependency-hints, verification-plan, required-evidence, and source-refs. Work-type is one of code-change, configuration-change, documentation-change, infrastructure-change, migration, operational-readiness, or test-change; upstream requirements and user stories are reached transitively through acceptance-criterion-refs rather than direct requirement-refs or user-story-refs.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Validate positive and negative closed-schema fixtures for all thirteen fields, reject every additional property including requirement-refs and user-story-refs, verify the closed work-type and capability values, and prove transitive upstream lineage through each acceptance-criterion-ref.

nonFunctionalRequirements.statement: A graph-aware successful result must checkpoint the exact validated update before one atomic merge and must return a proof bound to the resulting graph lineage.
nonFunctionalRequirements.measure: Successful graph-aware executions whose update checkpoint, merge receipt, and resulting snapshot verify as one exact lineage.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: 100 percent; partial or uncheckpointed merges are zero.

nonFunctionalRequirements.statement: Generic Core must resolve WorkBreakdown operations, adapters, contracts, and contributors through declared metadata without product identifiers or WorkBreakdown-specific branches.
nonFunctionalRequirements.measure: Product, adapter, operation, and contributor identifiers used in behavioral branches in generic Core.

nonFunctionalRequirements.statement: The same verified project state, exact invocation and configured adapter binding must select the same operation and enforce the same validation and drift result.
nonFunctionalRequirements.measure: Repeated routing, preflight, validation and drift decisions that match for identical content-addressed inputs.

nonFunctionalRequirements.statement: Every work item, coverage disposition, adapter result, source reference, traceability update and execution proof must be attributable to exact immutable inputs without conversational memory.
nonFunctionalRequirements.measure: Successful candidates whose domain entities and merge proof resolve to exact source artifacts and declared locations.

nonFunctionalRequirements.statement: A durably checkpointed WorkBreakdown execution must be revalidated and replayed for the exact invocation without reinvoking its adapter.
nonFunctionalRequirements.measure: Exact checkpoint replays producing the validated terminal result with zero additional adapter invocations.

constraints.statement: A WorkBreakdown adapter cannot receive graph service access, create graph nodes, choose graph relationship kinds, or submit graph mutations.
constraints.rationale: Only a trusted versioned contributor may translate a validated canonical domain candidate into graph assertions.

constraints.statement: WorkBreakdown may propose dependency hints but cannot emit or validate the authoritative dependency DAG.
constraints.rationale: WorkDependencyAnalysis owns ordering, cycle rejection, missing-dependency detection, and impossible-ordering policy.

constraints.statement: Assignment, ownership, estimates, scheduling, execution status, produced changes, completion edges, and verification results remain downstream concerns.
constraints.rationale: WorkBreakdown defines actions; later modules order, assign, perform, and verify them.

constraints.statement: Baselines, explicit not-applicable dispositions, approved change packages, repository snapshots, capability catalogs, and traceability references must be immutable and content-addressed at invocation.
constraints.rationale: Deterministic routing and drift detection require exact current authority rather than labels such as previous or latest.

constraints.statement: WorkBreakdown must not execute work, build code, or claim that a planned action has been completed.
constraints.rationale: The module's sole purpose is to produce candidate actions for later deterministic lifecycle modules.

scope.statement: Provider-neutral WorkBreakdownAdapter binding plus bounded Spec Kit and OpenSpec default adapter manifests and conformance fixtures.
Canonical state, disposition, approved-change, capability-catalog, work-item, coverage, clarification, revision, draft, change-set, baseline, and diagnostic artifacts.
A separate deterministic WorkBreakdown Gate for scope coverage, work-item scope, and reference validity.
Pre-adapter exact baseline, disposition, approved-change-package, repository commit, and tree-digest drift detection.
State-driven establish-breakdown and decompose-change routing with explicit clarification, drift, unable, and failure outcomes.
Trusted deterministic projection of validated work candidates into planning-only TraceabilityGraph relationships and an exact merge proof.

Complete bounded WorkItemDrafts containing only id, objective, bounded-scope, deliverables, work-type, acceptance-criterion-refs, architecture-refs, contract-refs, required-capabilities, dependency-hints, verification-plan, required-evidence, and source-refs.

nonGoals.statement: Construct or validate the authoritative work dependency DAG.
Execute work, build code, or produce implementation change sets.
nonGoals.rationale: This belongs to WorkExecution and integration stages.

nonGoals.statement: Generate or approve interface and data contracts.
nonGoals.rationale: WorkBreakdown consumes approved contract context; ContractGeneration owns contract production.

nonGoals.statement: Reconstruct historical work for an existing project without an approved WorkBreakdownBaseline.
nonGoals.rationale: Such projects establish a current baseline from current approved scope only.

nonGoals.statement: Claim live Spec Kit or OpenSpec CLI interoperability from contract fixtures alone.
nonGoals.rationale: V1 bounded manifests and fixtures prove the boundary; live command adapters require separate evidence.

nonGoals.statement: Select a person, agent, model, provider, or specialist for a work item.
Own estimates, schedules, assignees, status, progress, completion, or verification evidence results.
nonGoals.rationale: Those concerns belong to downstream planning, execution, and verification modules.

terminology.definition: An immutable authorized delta containing approved requirements and architecture changes, an approved contract change when applicable, and relevant TraceabilityGraph references.
An invocation-pinned provider-neutral catalog of controlled capabilities a WorkItemDraft may require from a later specialist assignment.
An immutable resumable state artifact returned with a WorkBreakdown clarification request.
A complete accounting entry marking authorized scope planned, already-satisfied with evidence, or no-work-required with approval.
A proposed ordering or dependency observation that has no authority until validated by WorkDependencyAnalysis.
An explicit immutable request to revise a WorkBreakdown candidate without relying on an implicit previous draft.
A trusted versioned projector that derives allowed planning graph assertions from an already validated canonical work-breakdown candidate.
The exact approved current set of planned work against which future authorized changes are decomposed.
A candidate planned-work delta against an exact current WorkBreakdownBaseline and ApprovedChangePackage.
A complete candidate initial set of planned work for a project with no approved WorkBreakdownBaseline.
A bounded, traceable, independently executable and verifiable proposed action that has not been ordered, assigned, executed, or verified.

currentStatus.summary: WorkBreakdown 0.1.0 has completed interactive requirements clarification and is awaiting paired Requirements Gate promotion before ArchitectureDesign.

assumptions.statement: Current means the exact approved content-addressed baseline supplied to the invocation, never an unpinned latest alias.
V1 bounded Spec Kit and OpenSpec manifests and fixtures do not by themselves claim live upstream CLI execution.
WorkBreakdown 0.1.0 has not been published, so this requirements run may establish its first exact contract.
Decompose-change requires a current RepositorySnapshot; explicit repository ApprovedNotApplicable is supported only when establishing work for a project with no repository context.

The final authoritative WorkItemDraft field set includes stable id, verification-plan, and required-evidence and excludes direct requirement-refs and user-story-refs; upstream lineage is transitive through acceptance-criterion-refs.

dependencies: A future WorkDependencyAnalysis module or compatible downstream contract for authoritative ordering.
A separate WorkBreakdown Gate before candidate promotion.
Approved RequirementsBaseline, ProjectOverviewBaseline, and ArchitectureBaseline inputs.
DevRelay TraceabilityGraph contributor, checkpoint, merge, and ModuleExecutionRecord contracts.
Explicit contract and repository disposition contracts plus a provider-neutral capability catalog.
The generic ModuleDefinition, ModulePlugin, ModuleInvocation, ModuleResult, artifact, evidence, digest, routing, and checkpoint contracts.
risks: Adapter-native task formats may encourage product-specific semantics unless normalization remains strict.
Coverage accounting may become bureaucratic if dispositions are not derived and presented compactly.
Dependency hints could accidentally be treated as authoritative before WorkDependencyAnalysis.
Existing projects without a work baseline could trigger misleading historical reconstruction unless explicitly prohibited.
Overly broad work items would undermine independent execution and verification even if structurally valid.
Planning-edge names could imply completed implementation unless the trusted contributor restricts them to planned semantics.
Weak drift checks could decompose an approved change against stale baselines or repository state.
deliverables: Approved WorkBreakdown RequirementsBaseline and ProjectOverviewBaseline with a visible clarification record.
Canonical WorkBreakdown state, input, work-item, coverage, clarification, revision, draft, change-set, baseline, and diagnostic contracts.
Configured Spec Kit and OpenSpec bounded adapter manifests and conformance fixtures.
Deterministic WorkBreakdown Gate and baseline-promotion contract.
State routing, drift, contract validation, checkpoint, replay, negative, and Core-neutrality evidence.
Trusted WorkBreakdownTraceabilityContributor with planning-only relationships and merge proof.
WorkBreakdown module definition with establish-breakdown and decompose-change operations.
